title: 😂 1953: The Kingman Incident
description:
😂 1953: The Kingman Incident — The Comedy Cut
The year is 1953. America is thriving. Everyone is building bombs, drinking martinis, and wearing hats.
Meanwhile, 30,000 feet up, a family of alien tourists from Zeta Reticuli are arguing over navigation.
"I told you to use the warp-drive coordinates, Zorp! Not the scenic, 'smell-the-sulfur-on-Venus' route!"
"But Glorka, I wanted to see a test detonation! It was on that Travel Channel special, 'Earth: Loud Noises and Bad Hats'!"
Seconds later, an Upshot-Knothole nuclear test—the biggest, loudest flash of the week—goes off in Nevada. Their sleek, metallic disc, which runs on pure, frictionless vacuum energy, is instantly fried by a massive electromagnetic pulse (EMP).
The ship begins to drop.
"We lost thrust! We lost inertial dampeners! I think we lost the TV antenna! We're crashing! Brace for impact!"
The sophisticated alien tourists plow into a hillside near Kingman, Arizona. They are not dead, but they are mortified.
Glorka sighs. "Well, that's what we get for installing the third-party navigation app."
Zorp kicks the console. "It said 'Avoid Tolls'!"
Glorka points out the window. "Look. Now we've got an unauthorized detour to Nevada's Storage Unit. And I think I stained the seat covers."
Three days later, the Men in Black arrive. They are not shadowy government spooks; they are just junior analysts from the Bureau of Peculiar Events (BPE) who drew the short straw. They're sweating in their three-piece polyester suits, trying to look mysterious.
BPE Agent 1: "Okay, remember the briefing. If the locals ask, we're here about an unusually large, round tumbleweed."
BPE Agent 2: "Sir, that thing is the size of two Cadillacs kissing. And it smells like ozone and burnt toast."
BPE Agent 1: (Whispering into a radio) "Yeah, we're gonna need a bigger canvas. And someone bring the Glade Plug-Ins."
They find the aliens sitting outside the wreck, politely waiting, holding a handwritten sign: "Lost Our Keys. Need AAA (Alien Assistance Association). Cash Only."
The BPE agents stand there, slack-jawed, looking at the smooth metallic craft that defies physics and the grumpy alien couple demanding to know the exchange rate for the US Dollar to Galactic Credits.
The Kingman Incident wasn't a military secret. It was an intergalactic fender-bender handled by the two most underpaid agencies in the Southwest. The whole event was classified not because it revealed advanced technology, but because the government didn't want to admit that they had to pay $10,000 for an alien tow truck.
🎨
